# `octo/webhooks`

Add `octo/webhooks` to the `Octo-Capabilities` header to receive these fields.

## Contents

- [Endpoints](#endpoints)
- [Schemas introduced by this capability](#schemas-introduced-by-this-capability)
- [Source](#source)
- [Integration notes](#integration-notes)

## Endpoints

This capability unlocks 5 endpoint(s).

- **`DELETE /webhooks`**: Webhook By URL. Body `WebhookDeleteByUrlRequest`.
- **`GET /webhooks`**: List Webhooks.
- **`POST /webhooks`**: Create Webhook. Body `WebhookRequest`.
- **`DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`**: Delete Webhook. Body `WebhookDeleteByUrlRequest`.
  - **webhookId** (string, in path, required): Webhook identifier.
- **`PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`**: Update Webhook. Body `WebhookRequest`.
  - **webhookId** (string, in path, required): Webhook identifier.

## Schemas introduced by this capability

6 schema(s) exist only when `octo/webhooks` is active.

### `Webhook`

Required: `id`, `event`, `url`.

- **id** (string, required): Webhook identifier. Example: `"webhook_booking_update"`.
- **event** (string, required): Event value. Example: `"booking.updated"`.
- **url** (string (uri), required): Fully-qualified URL. Example: `"https://www.city-sightseeing.com"`.
- **capabilities** (string[], optional): List of capability values. Example: `["octo/pricing", "octo/offers", "octo/waivers"]`.
- **useContactLanguage** (boolean, optional): Whether use contact language is enabled. Example: `true`.
- **headers** (HttpHeaders, optional): Headers object.
- **retryOnError** (boolean, optional): Whether retry on error is enabled. Example: `true`.

### `WebhookDeleteByUrlRequest`

- **url** (string (uri), optional): Fully-qualified URL. Example: `"https://www.city-sightseeing.com"`.
- **event** (string, optional): Event value. Example: `"booking.updated"`.

### `WebhookDiffOperation`

Required: `op`, `path`.

- **op** (string, required): Op value. One of: `add`, `remove`, `replace`. Example: `"add"`.
- **path** (string, required): Path value. Example: `"path-example"`.
- **was** (string | number | integer | boolean | string[] | object, optional, nullable): Was value. Example: `"was-example"`.
- **value** (string | number | integer | boolean | string[] | object, optional, nullable): Value value. Example: `"value-example"`.

### `WebhookEventPayload`

- **event** (string, optional): Event value. Example: `"booking.updated"`.
- **webhook** (Webhook, optional): Webhook object.
- **supplier** (Supplier, optional): Supplier object.
- **order** (Order, optional): Order object.
- **booking** (Booking, optional): Booking object.
- **product** (Product, optional): Product object.
- **availability** (Availability, optional): Availability object.
- **diff** (WebhookDiffOperation[], optional): List of diff values.

### `WebhookList`

Array of [`Webhook`](#webhook) — a list response, no fields of its own.

### `WebhookRequest`

- **event** (string, optional): Event value. Example: `"booking.updated"`.
- **url** (string (uri), optional): Fully-qualified URL. Example: `"https://www.city-sightseeing.com"`.
- **useContactLanguage** (boolean, optional): Whether use contact language is enabled. Example: `true`.
- **headers** (HttpHeaders, optional): Headers object.
- **retryOnError** (boolean, optional): Whether retry on error is enabled. Example: `true`.

## Integration notes

From [docs.ventrata.com/capabilities/webhooks](https://docs.ventrata.com/capabilities/webhooks).
All paths are under `/octo`.

### The four events

- **order_update** — an order changed. `octo/cart` is **always added automatically** for this event.
- **booking_update** — a booking changed.
- **availability_update** — availability changed.
- **product_update** — a product changed.

### Capabilities come from the header, not the body

> `capabilities` come from the `Octo-Capabilities` header on create/update requests, not from
> request body fields.

And they are **recalculated on every update**: a `PATCH` sent without the header narrows the
webhook's capabilities silently. Always send the same `Octo-Capabilities` header on an update that
you sent on create.

This matters because the stored capabilities decide the shape of every future delivery.

### Deliveries are POST, and carry the full object

The HTTP method of a delivery is always `POST`. Unlike `octo/notifications`, which sends only
identifiers, a webhook payload carries the serialized object — and it is serialized by the same code
as the corresponding endpoint, with the webhook's stored capabilities switched on first:

| Payload key | Same shape as |
|---|---|
| `order` | `GET /orders/:orderId` |
| `booking` | `GET /bookings/:uuid` |
| `product` | `GET /products/:productId` |
| `availability` | one item from `GET /availability` |

So capability fields — content, pricing, extras, questions — appear in a delivery exactly as they
would in that endpoint's response. One parser handles both.

**One documented exception:** when `octo/cardPayments` is active, delivery serialization suppresses
card payment session generation, so a detailed `cardPayment` payload is not emitted. Fetch it via
`GET /card_payments/{cardPaymentId}` if you need it.

### `diff[]` tells you what changed

`diff` is emitted for `order_update`, `booking_update` and `product_update` — **not** for
`availability_update`. Each entry is a `WebhookDiffOperation`: `op` (`add`, `remove`, `replace`),
`path`, `was`, `value`. Use it to react to a specific change instead of re-diffing the whole object.

### Subscribing and unsubscribing

`POST /webhooks` to create, `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}` to update (all fields optional),
`GET /webhooks` to list the connection's webhooks, `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}` to remove one.
`DELETE /webhooks` removes by URL — **pass `url` as either a query parameter or a body field**.

Operational fields on the webhook object:

- **headers** — sent with every delivery; the documented example is
  `{"X-Webhook-Secret": "whsec_123456abcdef"}`. There is no signature scheme, so this shared secret
  is how you authenticate an incoming call.
- **retryOnError** — retry failed deliveries. Keep it on and make the endpoint idempotent.
- **useContactLanguage** — serialize the payload in the booking contact's language rather than the
  connection default.

### Webhooks or notifications

Webhooks carry the whole object plus a `diff`, and cover `order_update`. `octo/notifications` sends
identifiers only and covers three types. Choose one per integration: subscribing to both delivers
every change twice. See [NOTIFICATIONS.md](NOTIFICATIONS.md).
